What is Compound?

Compound is an algorithmic, autonomous interest rate protocol built on Ethereum — the protocol that coined the term "DeFi" for many. Instead of a centralized bank setting rates, mathematical formulas driven by supply and demand determine rates in real time, 24/7, with no human intervention.

The protocol operates as a suite of markets, each for a specific asset like USDC, ETH, DAI, or WBTC. Liquidity providers deposit assets into these markets and immediately begin earning a variable interest rate that compounds every block. Borrowers can over-collateralize their positions to borrow against their supplied assets, also paying algorithmic interest. The key innovation that made Compound revolutionary is that everything — deposits, borrows, interest accrual, and governance — happens automatically through smart contracts, with no intermediary.

The heart of Compound is the cToken system. When you supply USDC to Compound, you receive cUSDC tokens at a 1:1 ratio (initially). These cTokens are live receipts that represent your share of the USDC market. As interest accrues on the underlying pool, the exchange rate between cTokens and the underlying asset increases — meaning your cUSDC is always worth more USDC than you deposited. This is how your balance "compounds" automatically, without you doing anything. The same applies to cETH, cDAI, cUSDT, cWBTC, and all other cTokens.

Compound is also a governance powerhouse. The COMP token gives holders direct control over the protocol: interest rate models, risk parameters like collateral factors and liquidation thresholds, which assets get listed, and even treasury management. Over 400,000 COMP holders participate in on-chain voting. This is real, functional decentralized governance — not theoretical. The protocol has survived numerous market stress tests and continues to operate entirely as coded, upgraded only through voter-approved proposals.

What makes Compound especially elegant is its COMP liquidity mining program, which was the first major DeFi incentive experiment. When you supply or borrow on Compound, you earn COMP tokens pro-rata, creating a dual yield stream. The COMP rewards add a meaningful boost to effective supply/borrow APYs, which you can calculate below. This model of "governance as incentive" changed how protocols distribute tokens forever.

COMP Governance

Compound is governed by COMP token holders who vote on proposals to update the protocol.

📊

Proposal Lifecycle

Proposals go through a 2-day review period, then a 3-day voting window. Requires 400,000 COMP quorum to pass.

⚙️

Parameter Changes

Rates, collateral factors, liquidation thresholds, reserve factors — all voted on by COMP holders.

🗳️

Token Distribution

COMP distributes ~4.7M tokens/year to suppliers and borrowers pro-rata. ~400K COMP holders active in votes.

🔗

Permissionless Listing

Through governance, any asset meeting risk assessments can be listed. Over 10 assets currently supported.

Risk Factors

⚠️

Liquidation Risk

If your health factor drops below 1.0 due to collateral price drops, your position can be partially liquidated. Always maintain a healthy buffer above the liquidation threshold.

Smart Contract Risk

Compound's v2 contracts have been audited multiple times and hold billions in TVL. However, no smart contract is 100% safe — audits and bug bounties mitigate but don't eliminate this risk.

Glossary

cToken
The receipt token you receive when supplying assets. cUSDC, cETH, cDAI, etc. Your cToken balance is fixed, but its exchange rate against the underlying asset grows with interest.
Supply APY
The annual percentage yield you earn on supplied assets. This is the interest paid by borrowers, distributed to suppliers pro-rata, and compounds automatically via the cToken exchange rate.
Borrow APY
The annual interest rate you pay on borrowed assets. This rate is variable and changes based on utilization — the higher the market utilization, the higher your borrow rate.
Utilization Rate
The percentage of supplied capital that is currently lent out. High utilization = more supply for borrowers needed = higher rates. It's the primary driver of Compound's interest rate algorithm.
COMP Token
Compound's governance token. Earned by both suppliers and borrowers. Gives holders voting rights over protocol parameters, new listings, and treasury allocations. Currently distributing ~4.7M tokens per year.
Interest Rate Model
The mathematical formula that determines borrow rates. Compound uses a piecewise model: rates are low and flat below the kink (80% utilization), then rise steeply above it. This incentivizes liquidity when markets are stressed.
Kink
The inflection point in Compound's interest rate model at 80% utilization. Below the kink, rates rise slowly. Above the kink, the slope multiplier increases ~5x, making borrowing much more expensive to incentivize supply.
Reserve Factor
A percentage of borrower interest that goes to the protocol's reserve treasury rather than suppliers. Currently set at 10-20% for most markets. These reserves serve as a safety backstop and can be used for upgrades or buybacks.
Health Factor
Your collateral value divided by your borrowed value. Below 1.0 means liquidation. A health factor of 2.0 means your collateral is worth 2x your borrowed position — a common safe target.
